newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sees extra $7 bln from power plant sales.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sees extra $7 bln from power plant sales.

text.p: Turkey is planning to earn $7 billion from privatising and leasing several power plants next year, a government minister said on Thursday.
"By privatising.... power plants through leasing, the government will obtain an additional $7 billion next year," the government spokesman Ziyattin Tokar told reporters.
He said the plants to be leased would be projects either already completed or those near completion.
"The incomplete ones will be completed by the lessee," he said. He did not give further details.
Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said earlier on Thursday the government's forecast of revenues from privatisation by the end of 1997 would be doubled to $13 billion.

The country's ten-year old privatisation programme has been stalled repeatedly by political opposition and legal obstacles. Turkey has raised some $3 billion through sell-offs since the programme started in 1986.

Sell-off revenues have in the past fallen far short of government forecasts, but the Islamist-led coalition under Erbakan has said privatisation is a priority in its aim to raise badly-needed revenues.
